summary: Most consequential: the Urgent rule drops the red-box criterion 'Hb < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man)', so jaundice with anaemia never triggers urgent referral. The footnote-3 atazanavir exception is also lost, so any medication (including atazanavir, which the page routes to p131) triggers Urgent. Smaller points: Venous stasis (finding) is a generic venous concept where Stasis dermatitis or Venous stasis syndrome is closer, tinea versicolor's dark patches are limited to the trunk (the page also says neck and upper arms), and the page's 'Hepatitis A IgM positive → acute hepatitis A infection' is not encoded as a diagnosis.
